title: fix(app-shell): page scope collects the missed object arms; interface list reuses the package scope (objectui#12980)
body:
Part of #12980
Clause-②: no

Part 5 of #12980: part 1's object-scope leftovers 2 and 3 (ACCEPT `6253365954`, contract review `6253321662` items ① 7 and ① 9). This PR does not close the card. Its leftover 1 (the chrome hooks in a package-less app) and the card's items 2 and 3 are not addressed here.

## What changed

**Leftover 2: the object arms the page derivation missed.** `pageObjectNames` (`packages/app-shell/src/console/appObjectScope.ts`) now also collects each arm below. Each one was checked against the renderer that reads it:

| Arm | Renderer read | Collected |
|---|---|---|
| `data.object` when `data.provider === 'object'` (the `ViewDataSchema` object arm on `object-grid` / `object-map` / the other view-data blocks) | `resolveRecordSourceObjectName` in `@object-ui/core`, the record source every view-data block resolves first | yes |
| `element:metadata_viewer` `properties.object` | `StateMachineView` reads it with `useMetadataItem('object', object)`. `FlowView` and `PermissionView` do not read it | yes, only when `properties.type === 'state_machine'` |
| `record:line_items` `properties.childObject` | `LineItemsPanel`: `find(childObject)` / `getObjectSchema(childObject)` | yes |
| `record:line_items` `properties.parentObject` | `LineItemsPanel`: the parent leg of the save batch (`buildMasterDetailEditBatch`) | yes |
| `parentDataSource.object` (`record:related_list`'s parent binding) | `ParentRecordBinding` resolves it on render | yes (bounded in-place fix, see Acceptance notes) |
| `addPicker.object` as the card spells it, i.e. `record:related_list` `add.picker.object` | `RelatedList` reads it only once the user opens the picker (`pickerOpen` gate), through the data adapter | **no**: it is never read while the page renders, and collecting it would hold the route on a read the open does not use |

The derivation reads only string values. An expression envelope, a non-string, a `data` array of pre-fetched records (the `object-calendar` arm) and any other `data` provider bind nothing. The per-block arms live in a `Map` keyed by block type, so a prototype key such as `toString` cannot match.

`PageView` needs no change because it reads the same derivation through `readPageObjectScope`.

**Leftover 3: `InterfaceListPage`'s second read.** The list page now finds the app the same way `nav:menu` does (`useParams().appName`, else `useNavigationContext().currentAppName`, matched over the active apps). It reads its source as `readObjectScope({ packageId, names: [source] })` when the app names a package, and as `{ names: [source] }` otherwise. `readObjectScope` itself is unchanged.

## Premises, measured

- **P1 (leftover 2).** With the new arm collection removed (the ablation below, i.e. main's derivation), a page that binds objects only through these arms draws first with each arm object unknown. `recordHref` returns `''` for each one, so the object is read by name on demand. None of the arms was already collected some other way.
- **P2 (leftover 3).** Yes, it is a second request. In a package app the route's `object?package=app.crm` already returned the source. Without the `packageId` pass, the list page then issues `object/crm_account` again. The cause: the names-only scope is a separate scope entry, and the package list does not fill the provider's by-name cache.

## Pins

- (a) `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/AppContent.pageScopeArms-12980.test.tsx` runs the real `MetadataProvider`, `AppContent` and `PageView`. A page binds five objects of another package, and only through the new arms. Every arm object is known on the page's first render. Each one is read once, by name, beside the package list, and there is no whole-registry `meta/object`.
- (a) `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/pageObjectNames.arms-12980.test.ts` is a unit pin for each arm. It also pins what is not collected: `add.picker.object`, a non-state-machine viewer, expression envelopes, non-strings, the `value` arm, a `data` array, and a prototype-key block type.
- (b) and (c) are in `packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/InterfaceListPage.packageScope-12980.test.tsx`, which uses the real `MetadataProvider` with the real `readPageObjectScope` as the route's half. (b) In a package app, the object calls are exactly `object?package=app.crm`. (c) CONTROL: in an app with no package, the call is exactly `object/crm_account`, once.
- (c) CONTROL: the #12811 app-route call set in `AppContent.pageRouteObjects-12980` is unchanged (green, including during ablation A).

## Ablations (one per half; restore proven by blob hash)

Both ablations ran through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, under the shared verify lock:

- **A: new arm collection dropped** (`appObjectScope.ts` back to main's `dataSource`-only lines). Anchor 1 to 0, blob `8c64252eae8c` to `c37798f6a25d`. Result: (a) red (the first-render hrefs were all `''`), 4 of the 6 unit pins red (the 2 negative pins stay green, as expected), and the `pageRouteObjects-12980` CONTROL green. Restored: blob `8c64252eae8c` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **B: `packageId` pass dropped** (`InterfaceListPage.tsx` back to `{ names: [cfg.source] }`). Blob `3b887aa20866` to `1f1156780f8e`. Result: (b) red (it received the extra `object/crm_account`), (c) CONTROL green. Restored: blob `3b887aa20866` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Gates (at `3c48263b22`)

- Closure build `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: 28/28 tasks, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. The three new test files are in the test project (`--listFilesOnly`).
- Targeted vitest (`--maxWorkers=1`) over the new and edited tests plus every test file naming `pageObjectNames`, `appObjectScope`, `pageRouteObjects-12980`, `pageObjectReads-12980`, `InterfaceListPage` or `namesOnlyScope`: 39 files, 611 tests passed. **The whole `packages/app-shell/` directory is declared to CI** and was not run locally.
- Lint, narrowed to the 11 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files with `eslint --no-inline-config --format json`: 11 files, 0 errors, 110 warnings (`no-explicit-any` and the like, the files' existing style). Type-aware linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.js` (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.
- Pre-tsc battery, each exit 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:doc-example-readers`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:icon-record-names`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:control-bytes`, `check-hand-rolled-comment-mask.mjs`.
- `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations): exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- **Bounded in-place fix: `parentDataSource.object`.** It is not on the order's list. It is the same defect class (an `ElementDataSourceSchema` object arm the derivation skipped), the fix is mechanical (one key added beside `dataSource`), it is in the same claimed file, and the same pins cover it. Evidence: `ParentRecordBinding` resolves it on render, and the unit pin and pin (a) bind it.
- **Not collected: `add.picker.object`.** See the table. The card's spelling `addPicker.object` does not exist in `@objectstack/spec` or in any renderer; the real key is `add.picker.object`. If the seat prefers to collect it anyway, it is a one-entry addition to `BLOCK_OBJECT_ARMS`.
- **Six test files beside `InterfaceListPage.tsx` were edited**: their hand-written `react-router-dom` mocks now name `useParams` (one line each). Before that, 31 tests in those six files failed with `No "useParams" export is defined on the "react-router-dom" mock`.
- The order's lock section says no whole-package-directory runs, while its gates section says to run each touched package's directory under the lock. I followed the lock section and declared the directory to CI.
